Q: Create a custom cast (that also accepts $null) A:

tl;dr

  • You can only achieve what you want via a constructor, not also with a cast.

  • Thus, your only options are:

    # Method syntax
[Checkbox]::new($null).ToString()

# New-Object alternative (more awkward)
(New-Object Checkbox @($null)).ToString()

Casts in PowerShell do double duty in PowerShell:

  • Type conversion, similar to C#, for instance, but with much more flexibility. This includes both true conversions from one type to another (e.g. [int] 1.1) as well as casting to a specific interface in the context of .NET method overload resolution (e.g. [System.Collections.IDictionary] @{ foo=42 }; see also below).

  • Instance construction: unlike in C#, cast syntax can situationally construct instances of the specified type, depending on the available constructors and the cast argument.

However, type-conversion casts take precedence and [Checkbox] $null is a valid "conversion": since your custom [Checkbox] type is (invariably) a .NET reference type, $null can be cast to it, and the result of this expression is simply $null.

As for the usefulness of such casts: Given that $null has no inherent type, something like [Checkbox] $null can guide overload resolution in .NET method calls, i.e. to unambiguously call the intended overload among multiple ones.

Q: How do I forbid an iFrame from scrolling its parent window? A:

Another hack: make a fully functional html page consisting only of empty head, body, and code for your iframe including the #URL. Make a data URI out of it (take the source for that page, convert to base64, and prefix it with 'data:text/html;base64,') and use that for the source of your iframe. For me, that stopped the obnoxious scrolling of the parent page. (Also I discovered that waiting a few seconds does work on Chrome, and rumor has it the behavior is not evident using Safari).

Here it is in action. I didn't bother to fix the double borders caused by the double iframing. Tell me if that works for you when you visit it.

Q: How can I display text when hovering over a legend item in Python Plotly? A:

Based on @r-beginners comment above it does not seem that at this time we can hover over legend entries in Python.

My current workaround is to use the long name, but place the legend above the plot. Here is an example using my workaround.

import plotly.graph_objects as go

trace_0_name = "the y value is the square of x"
trace_1_name = "the y value is the cube of x"
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[1,2,3], y=[1,2**2,3**2], name=trace_0_name))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[1,2,3], y=[1,2**3,3**3], name=trace_1_name))
fig.update_layout(legend=dict(yanchor='bottom', y=1.0, x=0))
fig.show()
